parameters.content:
# Onboard subscribers: Airtable

**Pattern:** Drip Sequence · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers inbox-triage work end to end across Airtable, Microsoft Teams and Slack.

It moves through 17 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Stamp & Shape Email
3. Payload Valid?
4. Record Rejected Input
5. Segment Audience
6. Step 1 — Welcome (Microsoft Teams)
7. Tag for Slow Nurture
8. Wait Before Step 2
9. Converted Already?
10. Step 2 — Value Nudge (Microsoft Teams)
11. Mark Converted — Stop Drip
12. Wait Before Final Step
13. Step 3 — Final Offer (Microsoft Teams)
14. Update Drip Status
15. Summarize Run Stats
16. Append Audit Row (Airtable)
17. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Microsoft Teams — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing inbox-triage work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Stamp & Shape Email → Payload Valid? → Record Rejected Input → Segment Audience → Step 1 — Welcome (Microsoft Teams) → Tag for Slow Nurture → Wait Before Step 2 → Converted Already? → Step 2 — Value Nudge (Microsoft Teams) → Mark Converted — Stop Drip → Wait Before Final Step → Step 3 — Final Offer (Microsoft Teams) → Update Drip Status → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Airtable) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Microsoft Teams

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Airtable and Microsoft Teams aligned by hand for inbox triage
- Inbox triage sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before Airtable
- Inbox triage work where "Stamp & Shape Email" is still a manual step before Airtable
- Inbox triage work that only reaches Airtable on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Airtable and Microsoft Teams in step for inbox triage, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Airtable or Microsoft Teams call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this inbox-triage build
- The pause before Airtable is durable — a inbox-triage run survives a restart
- Fans the same result out to Slack in the same run, for inbox triage
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 19 nodes for inbox triage before wiring Airtable

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Airtable PAT; Microsoft OAuth2; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Every step checks 'Converted Already?' before sending — a drip campaign that keeps emailing someone who already bought is the fastest way to burn trust. The Wait node's durable resume state (via `webhookId`) is what lets a multi-day wait survive an n8n restart instead of being held only in memory.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Add a 4th drip step with its own wait/exit-check pair.
2. Manually flip a test record's status to 'converted' mid-drip and confirm the ladder stops sending.
3. Shorten the wait durations so the full ladder runs in minutes instead of days, for testing.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
_Gotcha:_ Graph throttles with HTTP 429 — the retry setting on this node already handles it.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your inbox triage process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.
- Microsoft Teams: restrict the app registration to the target team; tenant-wide permission is not needed to post.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
inbox-triage payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
